rv.q: With a book by Emerald Fennell, who won an Oscar for the screenplay of Promising Young Woman, this reboot of the story, starring Carrie Hope Fletcher, delivers a 21st-century take on romance. And it's simply joyous. We all know Lloyd Webber can do portentous.
Cinderella is a triumph of catchy songs and fabulous wigs - it shouldn't be denied to a joy-starved public.
Lord Lloyd-Webber's richly enjoyable orchestrations range from grand waltzes, courtly processionals and marches to deftly pastiched and deeply felt romanticism.
Easily one of Lloyd Webber's most entertaining musicals - a family-friendly extravaganza, with larger-than-life characters that make up for our lost pantomime season in 2020.

On a scale of ashen rags to glass slippers, this Cinderella – amusing, unexpected, enjoyable – falls somewhere in the middle.
Sometimes Butler’s story gets bogged down while trying to nail each plot point, but it’s a genuinely innovative riff on the original.
This 'Cinderella' is a decent effort at a reinvention; but the mixed results don’t entirely justify pushing the barge out.
Andrew Lloyd Webber and Emerald Fennell’s show is visually spectacular, but lacks the consistent material to support its ideas.
The entire score is full of Lloyd Webber earworms, and I defy you to leave the theatre without humming any of them.
The long-awaited show from the 73-year-old industry veteran turns out to have been worth the wait.

But the ambition in taking on one of the most loved fairytales of all, one we’re pretty much born knowing, and reconstructing it for the 21st century, is lost in a book that cannot resolve the contradictions inherent in its avowed iconoclasm.

This new and exciting version of Cinderella is an absolute joy from start to finish. ... If you want to have yourself a merry little Christmas, a good start would be to treat yourself and the family to an evening at this wonderfully done show.

cn.t: Lloyd Webber's sassy, contemporary reimagining earns mostly positive reviews for its witty book, enjoyable score, and star Carrie Hope Fletcher, though some critics find the material inconsistent beneath the visual spectacle.
